item.title: #3619804: Remove unused templates from the Admin theme
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Minor task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +0/−158 · twig +0/−158
  • Diff: 41e2e84
  • Discussion: #3619804 · 7 contributors · 22 comments
  • Followers: 10
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Drupal core's experimental "Default Admin" theme (successor to the Gin admin theme merge) shipped with several Twig template overrides that were never actually reachable: menu-region--top.html.twig, menu-region--middle.html.twig, and menu-region--bottom.html.twig had no matching theme hook to attach to and were removed. Two other templates, page--clone.html.twig and page--group.html.twig, were reachable, but only via Drupal's automatic page template suggestions for paths that core itself doesn't provide: they exist to support the contrib Group and Quick Node Clone modules' /group/* and */clone pages. Sites that use Default Admin together with either of those contrib modules will now see those pages rendered with the normal page template instead of the node-edit-style layout Default Admin previously applied. A sixth template, input--submit--paragraph-action.html.twig, only overrode a render suggestion generated by the contrib Paragraphs module and is also removed. No core-only site (not running Group, Quick Node Clone, or Paragraphs) will notice any change.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Investigation (in comments) traced each template's theme hook registration. default_admin declares no hook_theme() of its own, and its hook_theme_registry_alter() only repoints the toolbar and menu__toolbar hooks at templates/navigation; the Navigation module's hook_theme() registers top_bar*, block__navigation, navigation_menu, navigation_content_top, and navigation__messages, none of which is a menu_region base hook. With no base hook and no Twig include/embed referencing them anywhere in core, menu-region--top.html.twig, menu-region--middle.html.twig, and menu-region--bottom.html.twig could never render, and the commit (41e2e84c) deletes all three along with their containing directory logic.

page--clone.html.twig and page--group.html.twig are different: Drupal resolves page template suggestions from the URL alias/path pattern regardless of whether a hook is declared, so these were live for any site running the contrib Group or Quick Node Clone modules, which have /group and */clone routes respectively. Both files were just one-line {% extends '@default_admin/page/page--node.html.twig' %} wrappers. Since core doesn't ship those routes itself, the templates were judged out of scope for core and removed, leaving those contrib integrations without special-cased layout support in Default Admin. input--submit--paragraph-action.html.twig was likewise a one-off override of an input suggestion generated only by the contrib Paragraphs module and was folded into the same cleanup. A related follow-up, #3621155, was opened to remove contrib-specific CSS selectors (Paragraphs, Smart Date, Inline Entity Form, Views Bulk Operations) left over in the same theme.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 29, 2026
  • Committed: September 8, 2026 (9 days and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • mherchel (Dripyard)
  • f0ns (Webhaven)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

f0ns did the legwork of tracing each template's theme hook registration to establish that the three menu-region templates were genuinely dead code, and flagged menu-region--bottom.html.twig as likely being in the same situation. When longwave also flagged page--clone.html.twig and page--group.html.twig as apparently unused, f0ns pushed back with a more careful explanation: those two are reachable through Drupal's automatic page-template-suggestion mechanism for contrib module routes (Group, Quick Node Clone), so removing them is an intentional behavior change for contrib users rather than dead-code cleanup, and initially argued for handling them in a separate issue. catch asked directly whether the issue should absorb that scope or spin off a new one, and longwave countered that core support for contrib modules' templates was never appropriate in the first place, since these templates were leftovers from when Gin was a contrib theme. f0ns accepted that reasoning, broadened the issue's scope, and pushed the additional removals (including the two page templates and the paragraph action input template) into the same MR.

item.title: #3561302: Register equivalent updates on site install
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +150/−24 · php +145/−24 · yml +5
  • Diff: 1ab223a
  • Discussion: #3561302 · 9 contributors · 33 comments
  • Followers: 10
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 9 contributors

Summary

Drupal tracks "equivalent updates" so that a database update backported to an older, still-supported branch is recognized as equivalent to the update that originally shipped it in a newer branch, preventing confusing warnings or double-running of updates. Previously this registration only happened when the corresponding hook_update_N() actually ran through update.php, but hook_update_N() functions never run on a brand-new site install. That meant a site installed directly on the older version (e.g. 10.4) never got the equivalent update recorded, so it could later show incorrect "you are trying to go backwards" warnings once it was upgraded past the version containing the original update. This fix registers those equivalent updates during module installation too, so freshly installed sites behave the same as sites that arrived at that version through running updates.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Calling UpdateHookRegistry::markFutureUpdateEquivalent() without the new $module and $ran_update_number arguments is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and will be required in drupal:13.0.0; the method is now @internal, use the #[MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent] attribute instead (see #3617733).
  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Update\Attribute\MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent PHP attribute for hook_update_N() functions, letting the update be registered as equivalent even when the function never runs (e.g. on a fresh site install).

Technical details

The mechanism is a new #[MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent(futureUpdateNumber, futureVersionString)] PHP attribute applied directly to a hook_update_N() function, replacing the old pattern of calling \Drupal::service('update.update_hook_registry')->markFutureUpdateEquivalent() from inside the update function body. Because attributes can be discovered by reflection without invoking the function, ModuleInstaller::doInstall() now loops through every available update number returned by updateRegistry->getAvailableUpdates($module) during install, reflects each {$module}_update_{$version} function with ReflectionFunction, and if it carries the attribute, calls markFutureUpdateEquivalent() on its behalf, wrapping the reflection/registration in a try/catch that logs via Error::logException(). The same reflection check was added to update_do_one() in update.inc so the attribute also drives registration when updates run through update.php (previously that path relied on the explicit service call still present in the update function body).

UpdateHookRegistry::markFutureUpdateEquivalent() gained two new parameters, $module and $ran_update_number, currently accepted only via func_get_args() (commented out in the signature) to avoid a hard API break; calling it the old way now triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice and falls back to determineModuleAndVersion(). The method is documented @internal since the attribute is now the supported way to register these. Core's own system.install equivalent-update declarations and the equivalent_update_test fixture module were converted to use the attribute, and a new equivalent_update_test_attribute_install test module and testAttributeOnInstall() test verify the install-time registration path.

Upgrade

Replace direct calls to markFutureUpdateEquivalent() inside an update function body with the attribute:

use Drupal\Core\Update\Attribute\MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent;

#[MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent(11101, '11.1.1')]
function my_module_update_10400(): void {
  // The function can be no-op.
}

Calling \Drupal::service('update.update_hook_registry')->markFutureUpdateEquivalent(11101, '11.1.1') directly from inside the update function still works but is deprecated and will require the $module and $ran_update_number arguments in Drupal 13 (see #3617733 and the change record at drupal.org/node/3572245).

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: December 3, 2025
  • Committed: September 7, 2026 (9 months and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • godotislate
  • xjm (Zoocha)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)

Collaboration

godotislate's initial proposal to solve this with a pair of attributes (MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent/CheckEquivalentUpdate) was discussed against an alternative catch raised, hard-coding equivalent branch numbers directly in update.php and site install, as brought up by xjm in Slack, before the reflection-based attribute approach was pursued in the MR. After review, alexpott pushed for the direct-call convention to be deprecated and markFutureUpdateEquivalent() marked @internal since "there is no reason to call it" once the attribute exists, which godotislate implemented and followed up on by filing #3617733 to make the new $module/$ran_update_number parameters required in Drupal 13. quietone later made substantial edits to the change record, trimming it to focus on the change itself and the action sites need to take, after noting a good example communicates more than lengthy prose.

item.title: #3452493: Remove images that have been replaced with svg files
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 46 files, +0/−0 · gif +0 · png +0
  • Diff: f6b57b5
  • Discussion: #3452493 · 6 contributors · 17 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

Drupal core has removed 46 legacy image files (GIFs and PNGs) that were left behind after earlier issues replaced them with SVG versions: the ajax throbber and loading indicators in core/misc, and the file-type icon sets (PDF, text, audio, spreadsheet, etc.) shipped with the Claro theme, the Umami demo theme, and Starterkit theme. The SVG replacements have been in use since Drupal 11, so this is cleanup of now-dead files rather than a behavior change for standard sites. It only matters if a custom theme, override, or piece of custom CSS still points directly at one of the removed file paths.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Removed 46 legacy raster image files (the ajax throbber/loading indicators in core/misc, and file-type icon sets in Claro, Umami, and Starterkit) that had already been superseded by SVG equivalents; any code still referencing the old .gif/.png paths must switch to the .svg files of the same name.

Technical details

The removed files are core/misc/loading-small.gif, core/misc/loading.gif, core/misc/throbber-active.gif, and core/misc/throbber-inactive.png, plus 14 file-type icons each (application-pdf, text-html, x-office-document, etc.) under core/profiles/demo_umami/themes/umami/images/classy/icons/, core/themes/claro/images/classy/icons/, and core/themes/starterkit_theme/images/icons/. In every case an SVG file of the same base name already exists in the same directory (e.g. core/misc/throbber-active.svg, core/themes/claro/images/classy/icons/application-pdf.svg), added by prior issues #2575253, #1974928, and #3521857. No template, library, or CSS file needed updating in this commit because those consumers had already been switched over to the SVG assets in those earlier issues; this change is purely deleting the now-orphaned raster files.

Upgrade

Any custom theme, template override, or CSS that hardcodes a path to one of the removed files (for example core/themes/claro/images/classy/icons/application-pdf.png or core/misc/throbber-active.gif) will 404 after upgrading. Update those references to the SVG file of the same name in the same directory, e.g.:

core/misc/throbber-active.gif      -> core/misc/throbber-active.svg
core/themes/claro/images/classy/icons/application-pdf.png -> core/themes/claro/images/classy/icons/application-pdf.svg

Contribution

  • Committed: September 7, 2026 (2 years and 2 commits later)

item.title: #2025089: Deprecate user_role_grant_permissions(), user_role_revoke_permissions() and user_role_change_permissions()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 43 files, +354/−173 · php +354/−173
  • Diff: 0f7caab
  • Discussion: #2025089 · 12 contributors · 72 comments
  • Followers: 18
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 12 contributors

Summary

Drupal has long had three procedural helper functions for adding, removing, or bulk-changing the permissions on a user role: user_role_grant_permissions(), user_role_revoke_permissions(), and user_role_change_permissions(). These are now deprecated in favor of equivalent methods directly on the role entity's RoleInterface. Core's own call sites (tests, filter.module, the permissions form, and several contrib-adjacent modules) have all been converted to the new object-oriented API. Sites and contributed modules that call the old functions will get a deprecation notice and must switch before Drupal 13, where the functions are removed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: user_role_grant_permissions(), user_role_revoke_permissions() and user_role_change_permissions() are deprecated in favor of RoleInterface::grantPermissions(), RoleInterface::revokePermissions() and RoleInterface::changePermissions().
  • New API: RoleInterface gains grantPermissions(array $permissions), revokePermissions(array $permissions) and changePermissions(array $permissions) methods for bulk permission changes on a role entity.

Technical details

RoleInterface gains three new methods: grantPermissions(array $permissions): static, revokePermissions(array $permissions): static, and changePermissions(array $permissions): static. The existing singular grantPermission() and revokePermission() methods on Role are now thin wrappers that cast their argument to an array and delegate to the new plural methods, so no behavior changes there. changePermissions() (previously only a procedural function's logic) is now a first-class interface method: it filters the given associative array into permissions to grant versus revoke and calls the other two methods accordingly.

The three deprecated procedural functions in user.module now load the role with \Drupal::entityTypeManager()->getStorage('user_role')->loadOverrideFree($rid), call the corresponding new RoleInterface method, save, and emit an E_USER_DEPRECATED trigger_error. Call sites throughout core (comment, file, filter, image, media, node, responsive_image, system, taxonomy, user tests, and filter.module's FilterFormat::postSave() and the permissions form submit handler) were updated to the pattern Role::loadOverrideFree($rid)->grantPermissions([...])->save() (or revokePermissions()/changePermissions()), replacing direct calls to the deprecated functions. See #3620216 for the loadOverrideFree()/loadMultipleOverrideFree() API this conversion depends on.

Upgrade

Replace calls to the deprecated procedural functions with the equivalent RoleInterface methods on a loaded role entity:

// Before:
user_role_grant_permissions($rid, ['administer nodes']);
user_role_revoke_permissions($rid, ['administer nodes']);
user_role_change_permissions($rid, ['administer nodes' => TRUE, 'access content' => FALSE]);

// After:
use Drupal\user\Entity\Role;

Role::loadOverrideFree($rid)->grantPermissions(['administer nodes'])->save();
Role::loadOverrideFree($rid)->revokePermissions(['administer nodes'])->save();
Role::loadOverrideFree($rid)->changePermissions([
  'administer nodes' => TRUE,
  'access content' => FALSE,
])->save();

Note loadOverrideFree() can return NULL if the role doesn't exist, so guard with ?-> where appropriate, as done in media_install() and node_install().

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 21, 2013
  • Committed: September 7, 2026 (13 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • andypost (Skilld)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • dcam
  • amateescu

Collaboration

The API shape was debated for years between andypost and alexpott: whether grantPermissions()/revokePermissions() should take an array argument or be variadic extensions of the singular methods, and whether the plural methods were even worth adding alongside the singular ones. alexpott argued a dedicated plural array-accepting method was clearer than overloading the singular method with variadic arguments, which andypost preferred for its type-safety of individual string arguments. When nicxvan picked up the implementation, they resolved the long-standing disagreement by following alexpott's array-based approach, and opened a follow-up (#3621087) to address the singular/plural question for UserCreationTrait separately. berdir's review noted the diff didn't change the actual list of permissions, only how the calls were made, and estimated contrib has roughly 700 call sites that would need similar conversion, suggesting Rector automation.

item.title: #2865710: Dependencies from only one instance of a widget are used in display modes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +446/−2 · php +417/−2 · yml +29
  • Diff: d496db0
  • Discussion: #2865710 · 17 contributors · 111 comments
  • Followers: 23
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 17 contributors

Summary

Entity view and form displays calculate their config dependencies from the widget and formatter plugins used on each field, so that deleting something a plugin depends on (a view mode, an image style, a taxonomy vocabulary, etc.) is blocked or handled safely. This calculation was broken whenever a display used the same plugin on more than one field: only the last field's dependencies were kept, so the others were silently dropped. A common trigger is two comment fields each set to show a different comment view mode, or two image fields using different image styles. If the missing dependency was later deleted, the display could break with a fatal error instead of being cleanly protected. Existing sites do not need to change anything, but should run database updates after upgrading so the new post update hooks can recalculate and fix the dependencies stored in their existing displays.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New field_post_update_recalculate_entity_form_display_dependencies() and field_post_update_recalculate_entity_view_display_dependencies() post update hooks resave all entity_form_display and entity_view_display config entities to recalculate their dependencies.

Technical details

EntityFormDisplay::getPluginCollections() and EntityViewDisplay::getPluginCollections() build a EntityDisplayPluginCollection keyed by $configuration['type'] (the plugin ID). When two fields on the same display use the same widget or formatter, the second field's configuration overwrote the first's in that array, so ConfigEntityBase::calculateDependencies(), which iterates the plugin collection to merge in each plugin's calculateDependencies() result, only ever saw one instance's dependencies. The fix rekeys both collections by $field_name instead of plugin type, which is guaranteed unique per display; calculateDependencies() never relied on the array keys, so this is safe.

Because existing config was calculated with the old, lossy keying, two new post update functions, field_post_update_recalculate_entity_form_display_dependencies() and field_post_update_recalculate_entity_view_display_dependencies(), use ConfigEntityUpdater to resave every entity_form_display and entity_view_display, forcing dependencies to be recalculated with the corrected code. Test coverage includes a new field_dynamic_dependencies_test module with a formatter/widget pair whose calculateDependencies() adds a configurable module dependency, used in EntityDisplayDependenciesTest to prove dependencies from multiple fields using the same plugin are all retained, plus RecalculateDependenciesUpdateTest to verify the update path against a pre-fix fixture.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 31, 2017
  • Committed: September 5, 2026 (9 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • hchonov (bio.logis Genetic Information Management GmbH)
  • dcam (USDA-ARS)
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • jofitz (ComputerMinds)
  • heatherwoz (University of Washington)
  • Adev22 (Google Code-In)
  • hctom (undpaul)
  • acbramley (PreviousNext)
  • bhanu951
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • james.williams (ComputerMinds)
  • james.nugent7
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)

Collaboration

The underlying rekeying fix (using field name instead of plugin type) was proposed early on by hchonov and james.williams, who then wrote the patch and tests over many reroll cycles. dcam reviewed extensively, confirmed the bug independently while building a contrib module (Entity Reference Facet Link) whose formatter depends on facet entities, and pushed for the update hook needed to repair already-broken production config, contributing draft code for it. larowlan's review pushed back on an early patch that refactored unrelated shared test code across EntityDisplayTest and EntityFormDisplayTest; james.williams agreed it had gone too far and reworked it into a narrower shared trait instead.

item.title: #3565781: Deprecate the Search module
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 60 files, +113/−54 · php +105/−2 · yml +8/−52
  • Diff: cdd4876
  • Discussion: #3565781 · 5 contributors · 36 comments
  • Followers: 9
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

The Search module (and its submodules that index content, users, and help) is now officially marked deprecated in Drupal core, following the policy decision made in #3476883 to move Search from core into a contributed project. Sites that currently have the Search module enabled will start seeing a deprecation notice, and should begin planning to migrate to a contributed search solution before Search is removed from a future core release. No functionality was removed yet: this issue only starts the formal deprecation clock and cleans up the codebase in preparation for eventual removal.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: The search, node_search, user_search, and help_search modules are now marked lifecycle: deprecated in their .info.yml files, per the decision in #3476883 to move Search from core to a contributed project.

Technical details

The change adds lifecycle: deprecated and lifecycle_link: https://www.drupal.org/node/3223395#s-search to the .info.yml files of search.module, node_search, user_search, and help_search, which is the standard Drupal core mechanism (per the module/theme removal process) for flagging an extension for future removal. Because installing or using a deprecated module now triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice via the module installer, every test in these four modules (and tests elsewhere that install them, such as SearchPageTest, the JSON:API/REST SearchPage* resource tests, and Olivero's testConfigSchema/testPreprocessBlock) gained the #[IgnoreDeprecations] PHPUnit attribute so the notices don't fail the test suite.

As part of the cleanup pass required before deprecation ("thorough search of core for any remaining references"), four leftover config fixture files (core.entity_view_mode.node.search_index.yml and core.entity_view_mode.node.search_result.yml, in both the multilingual and testing_config_install fixture sets) were deleted; investigation showed these view modes had no actual dependency on the Search module. Claro and Olivero's own search-related theme code was intentionally left in place because those two themes are themselves slated for deprecation, with separate follow-up issues (#3620801 for default_admin, #3620804 for Umami) handling their theme-specific references instead.

Upgrade

Modules or sites that depend on the search, node_search, user_search, or help_search modules should plan to migrate to a contributed replacement before these are removed from core. Contributed or custom code that installs one of these modules in tests should add the #[IgnoreDeprecations] PHPUnit attribute to avoid failures from the new deprecation notice, for example:

use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\IgnoreDeprecations;

#[Group('search')]
#[IgnoreDeprecations]
class MyCustomSearchTest extends BrowserTestBase {

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: January 6, 2026
  • First commit: September 4, 2026 (8 months later)
  • Last commit: September 5, 2026 (1 day and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • acbramley (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)

Collaboration

Getting this issue to a committable state took several rounds of tracking down stray references to Search across core. quietone repeatedly ran git grep for "search" and found leftover config fixtures (core.entity_view_mode.node.search_index.yml and related files) that acbramley then investigated, confirming via local test runs that they had no real dependency on the Search module and could simply be removed. After commit, longwave found the 11.x backport didn't cleanly cherry-pick, and quietone tracked down several tests still installing Search on 11.x because a related cleanup issue (#3575587) hadn't been backported, reopening it and preparing a fix so the backport could land. catch settled an open question about Claro and Olivero by deciding their search-related theme code did not need to be stripped out immediately, since both themes are themselves being deprecated, and opened separate follow-up issues for default_admin and Umami instead.

item.title: #3580705: Deprecate update.compare functions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 20 files, +997/−509 · php +996/−509 · yml +1
  • Diff: 2689e34
  • Discussion: #3580705 · 5 contributors · 45 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Three long-standing procedural functions in update.module, update_process_project_info(), update_calculate_project_data(), and update_calculate_project_update_status(), are now deprecated and will be removed in Drupal 13. They still work today, but calling them triggers a deprecation warning. Any custom code that inspects a site's available updates (custom update-status pages, contrib modules hooking into update checking, tests) should switch to the new calculateProjectData() method on the update manager service instead of calling the procedural function directly.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: update_process_project_info(), update_calculate_project_data(), and update_calculate_project_update_status() are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 (removed in 13.0.0) in favor of UpdateManagerInterface::calculateProjectData() and the internal UpdateCalculator service.
  • New API: UpdateManagerInterface::calculateProjectData(array $available): array was added as the public replacement for update_calculate_project_data().

Technical details

The three procedural functions keep working as thin wrappers: each triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED warning and then delegates to the new services. update_process_project_info() calls \Drupal::service(UpdateCalculator::class)->processProjectInfo(), update_calculate_project_data() calls the new UpdateManagerInterface::calculateProjectData(), and update_calculate_project_update_status() calls UpdateCalculator::updateProjectStatus().

UpdateManagerInterface::calculateProjectData(array $available): array, implemented on UpdateManager, is the one non-internal addition: it moves the logic previously in update_calculate_project_data() onto the manager, which already owns project storage and the update_project_data key/value cache. The rest of the logic moved into an @internal UpdateCalculator service (processProjectInfo() and updateProjectStatus()) plus two new @internal value objects, UpdateProject and UpdateServerProjectInfo (both \ArrayObject subclasses with createFromArray()/toArray()), which replace the loosely-typed arrays that update_calculate_project_update_status() previously mutated by reference.

UpdateManager::__construct() gained an optional ?UpdateCalculator $updateCalculator constructor parameter; omitting it (as any custom subclass still would) triggers a deprecation notice and falls back to \Drupal::service(UpdateCalculator::class). Separately, package_manager's ProjectInfo class had the UpdateManagerInterface dependency removed from its constructor since it now calls \Drupal::service(UpdateManagerInterface::class)->calculateProjectData() directly. A follow-up commit only corrected the change-record link in the deprecation messages (from node 3566774 to 3587768).

Upgrade

Replace direct calls to the deprecated functions:

// Before
$data = update_calculate_project_data($available);

// After
$data = \Drupal::service(\Drupal\update\UpdateManagerInterface::class)->calculateProjectData($available);

// Before
update_process_project_info($projects);

// After
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\update\UpdateCalculator::class)->processProjectInfo($projects);

update_calculate_project_update_status(&$project_data, $available) becomes UpdateCalculator::updateProjectStatus(), but its parameters changed type from arrays to value objects:

// Before
update_calculate_project_update_status($project_data, $available);

// After
$project_data = \Drupal::service(\Drupal\update\UpdateCalculator::class)
  ->updateProjectStatus(
    \Drupal\update\UpdateProject::createFromArray($project_data),
    \Drupal\update\UpdateServerProjectInfo::createFromArray($available)
  )->toArray();

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 22, 2026
  • Committed: September 4, 2026 (5 months and 4 commits later)

Key contributors

  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • amateescu

item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core

Summary

Drupal's schema definition API (introduced in #3411490) can now declare "generated" columns: columns whose value the database computes automatically from an expression over other columns, rather than one that application code writes. This was motivated by the need to index data inside JSON columns (see #3343634): since MariaDB doesn't support indexing arbitrary SQL expressions, the practical way to index derived data is to expose it as a generated column and index that. A generated column can be "stored" (computed on write and kept on disk, like a regular column) or "virtual" (computed on read, saving storage but not supported for indexing on PostgreSQL). This is a new opt-in capability for code that adopts the new schema API; it does not change any existing database table.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Column::generated() factory and Drupal\Core\Database\SchemaDefinition\GeneratedColumnStorage enum let schema definitions declare database-computed (generated) columns, stored or virtual.

Technical details

The core addition is Column::generated(), a static factory on the Column value object that requires a ColumnType, a GeneratedColumnExpression (a small Expression subclass holding the raw SQL expression text), and a GeneratedColumnStorage enum case (Virtual or Stored). Column::validate() rejects a generated expression on a Serial column, and Table::validate() rejects a generated column in the primary key, since MariaDB and SQLite don't allow that. Column::toArray() puts the whole Column object under the array spec's generated key, which the mysql, pgsql, and sqlite driver createFieldSql() implementations translate into GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) VIRTUAL|STORED clauses (with DEFAULT NULL suppressed for generated columns).

SQLite required the most work because it has no ALTER TABLE support for adding a STORED generated column (only VIRTUAL can be added in place; STORED forces the driver's usual create-new-table-and-copy-data path), and its PRAGMA table_info doesn't report generated columns at all. The driver's introspectSchema() now uses PRAGMA table_xinfo (which exposes a hidden flag distinguishing ordinary, virtual-table, VIRTUAL generated, and STORED generated columns) and, for generated columns, recovers the original column definition text by parsing the CREATE TABLE statement out of sqlite_master (new getColumnDefinitions(), splitColumnDefinitions(), skipQuotedRun(), skipComment() helpers), since SQLite exposes no pragma for a generated column's expression or storage kind. That recovered text is stored under a sqlite_definition key and reused verbatim by createFieldSql()/processField() on rebuild; if recovery fails, a SchemaException is thrown rather than silently dropping the column. Table rebuilds (alterTable()) also exclude generated columns from the data-copy mapping, since the database rejects writes to them.

Summary

On PostgreSQL 18+ (the minimum for Drupal 12), Drupal's Merge query (the "insert or update" helper used by core's key_value store, the locale module's string location tracking, and the taxonomy index that is rebuilt whenever a published node is saved) now executes as a single native SQL MERGE statement instead of a SELECT followed by a separate INSERT or UPDATE. This halves the number of database round trips for these operations and also closes a small race-condition window that existed in the old check-then-write approach. There is no API change and nothing for site owners or module authors to configure; PostgreSQL sites simply get faster, safer merge queries automatically. Benchmarks in the issue showed 14 to 18% less time per merge query on a low-latency connection, with larger savings expected when there is more network latency between the web and database servers.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The PostgreSQL driver gets a new \Drupal\pgsql\Driver\Database\pgsql\Merge class, returned by the driver's Connection::merge(), which extends the generic \Drupal\Core\Database\Query\Merge. Its __toString() builds a MERGE INTO {table} USING (SELECT 1) AS drupal_merge_source ON (...) statement with WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE and WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT clauses, ending in RETURNING merge_action(). executeNativeMerge() binds all placeholders (including blob fields, expressions, and select-expression arguments) and maps the returned merge_action() value ('INSERT'/'UPDATE') back to Merge::STATUS_INSERT or Merge::STATUS_UPDATE, returning NULL when the row matched but no update fields were supplied.

isNativeMerge() gates when the native path is used: the condition must target the merge table itself and there must be insert fields or default fields. Otherwise execute() falls back to the parent's generic SELECT + INSERT/UPDATE emulation, specifically when the condition targets another table (no ON clause possible), when there are no insert fields (no WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT possible), or when values are inserted into serial fields, since the generic insert path also synchronizes the table's sequence afterwards.

Because native MERGE under PostgreSQL's default READ COMMITTED isolation is still subject to a race where a concurrent transaction inserts the same row between the match phase and the write, execute() catches IntegrityConstraintViolationException and retries the statement once, so the now-existing row is matched and updated instead. item.title: #3615415: Remove using preg_replace() on every query for PostgreSQL
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task

Summary

On PostgreSQL, every single database query used to be passed through a preg_replace() call looking for LIKE and regular-expression operators so it could add a ::text type-cast to the field they act on (PostgreSQL doesn't auto-cast non-text columns for those operators). That regex ran on every query regardless of whether it used those operators, and it worked over the final SQL string so it could also mismatch inside expressions or string literals. This change moves the cast into query compilation, so it is only added to the specific conditions that need it, removing the per-query overhead for the many queries that never use LIKE or regex operators. Raw SQL strings (not built with the query builder) still get the old rewrite as a fallback, but relying on that is now deprecated since it will be removed in Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The array returned by Connection::mapConditionOperator() supports a new field_suffix key that Condition::compile() appends to the field before the operator; database drivers overriding the condition operator map should be aware of it.
  • Deprecation: Relying on the PostgreSQL driver's Connection::prepareStatement() to auto-add a ::text cast to fields used with LIKE/regex operators in raw SQL strings is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed in drupal:13.0.0.
  • New API: New public method Connection::getConditionFieldSuffix() returns the SQL suffix (e.g. a type-cast) a driver needs appended to a field for a given condition operator, for use when building raw SQL condition snippets.

Technical details

Condition::compile() now supports a field_suffix directive in the array returned by Connection::mapConditionOperator(), appended to the compiled field fragment before the operator. The PostgreSQL driver's $postgresqlConditionOperatorMap sets 'field_suffix' => '::text' for LIKE, LIKE BINARY, NOT LIKE, REGEXP and NOT REGEXP, plus identity entries for ILIKE, NOT ILIKE, ~* and !~* so code (such as Views' StringFilter) that builds conditions with those PostgreSQL-native operators directly also gets the cast.

For code that builds raw SQL condition snippets outside the query builder (e.g. Query::where()), a new Connection::getConditionFieldSuffix($operator) method exposes the same suffix so it can be added manually. pgsql\Connection::prepareStatement() keeps its old preg_replace() fallback for raw SQL, but now guards it behind a stripos()/str_contains() check so it only runs for strings actually containing LIKE or ~*, made the regex idempotent (skips fields already cast), and raises an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice when it rewrites a query, pointing at the change record for removal in Drupal 13. StringFilter's operator handlers (opEqual, opContains, opStartsWith, opEndsWith, opNotLike, opRegex, etc.) were updated to call getConditionFieldSuffix() and append it to the expression themselves, since they build raw where-expression snippets rather than using Condition::compile().

Upgrade

Custom database drivers that override mapConditionOperator() can add a field_suffix entry to have it appended to the field automatically during condition compilation.

Code that issues raw SQL strings against PostgreSQL using LIKE, NOT LIKE, ILIKE, REGEXP, or ~*/!~* should add the cast explicitly instead of relying on the driver to rewrite the query, since that fallback is deprecated and removed in Drupal 13:

$suffix = $connection->getConditionFieldSuffix('LIKE');
$query->where("[title]$suffix LIKE :pattern", [
  ':pattern' => '%foo%',
]);

Summary

Drupal core's bundled HTMX library has been upgraded from version 2 to the newly released version 4, which the HTMX project describes as a complete rewrite ("the fetch()ening"). Core's HTMX integration (the PHP Htmx attribute-builder class, the request-header helpers, FormBuilder's HTMX handling, and the client-side JavaScript that wires HTMX into Drupal's AJAX/behavior system) has been refactored to work with the new library. There are no visible UI changes for standard core usage, but sites with custom code, themes, or contrib modules that use HTMX attributes, HTMX request/response headers, or HTMX JavaScript extensions should review the published change record, since htmx 4 changes attribute names, header names and formats, event payloads, the extension registration API, and introduces a default 60 second request timeout and different history/back-navigation behavior.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: The bundled htmx.js/htmx.min.js vendor library is upgraded from 2.0.4 to 4.0.0, a rewrite with backward-incompatible changes to attributes, headers, events, and the extension API.
  • API change: The Drupal\Core\Htmx\Htmx factory class was substantially reworked for htmx 4: several methods were renamed or removed (e.g. disable()→ignore(), disabledElt()→disable(), request()→config(); ext(), disinherit(), history(), inherit(), params(), and prompt() were removed because those attributes no longer exist in htmx 4), most builder methods gained an int $modifiers parameter for the new :inherited/:append attribute modifiers, and new methods action(), method(), query(), and status() were added for new htmx 4 attributes. HtmxRequestInfoTrait methods were renamed to match new/changed HTMX headers: getHtmxTrigger() and getHtmxPrompt() are gone, getHtmxTriggerName() now parses the triggering element's name out of the new HX-Source header, and a new getHtmxRequestType() reads the HX-Request-Type header.
  • Deprecation: FormBuilderInterface::HTMX_REQUEST constant is deprecated in favor of HtmxRequestInfoTrait::isHtmxRequest().

Technical details

The core-side changes track htmx 4's rewrite closely. HtmxRequestInfoTrait was updated because htmx 4 replaces the old HX-Trigger/HX-Trigger-Name headers with HX-Source (a CSS-selector-like identifier for the triggering element, URI-encoded) and adds HX-Request-Type ("full" or "partial"); getHtmxTriggerName() now regex-extracts a name="..." fragment out of HX-Source instead of reading a dedicated header. FormBuilder::prepareForm() had a latent bug here: it still read the removed hx-trigger header directly (rather than through the trait), which meant $hx_trigger was always NULL and the out-of-band form_build_id swap fired unconditionally; this was caught during review and fixed to use getHtmxSource()/getHtmxTarget() via the newly-added HtmxRequestInfoTrait usage in FormBuilder.

The Htmx class (core/lib/Drupal/Core/Htmx/Htmx.php) gained self::INHERITED/self::APPEND bit-flag modifiers, threaded through nearly every builder method via a new keyWithModifiers() helper, to support htmx 4's explicit :inherited/:append attribute-inheritance syntax. Several methods for attributes htmx 4 removed (ext, disinherit, history, inherit, params, prompt) were removed outright, others were renamed to match new attribute names (disable()→ignore(), disabledElt()→disable(), request()→config()), and new methods (action(), method(), query(), status()) were added for htmx 4's new hx-action, hx-method, hx-query (supporting the HTTP QUERY method), and hx-status attributes. Deprecation shims for the removed/renamed methods were left to a follow-up issue rather than being part of this change.

On the client, core/misc/htmx/htmx-assets.js was rewritten to hook into htmx 4's new event/task model: Drupal.attachBehaviors/detachBehaviors are now triggered from htmx:before:swap/htmx:after:swap handlers that resolve the correct DOM context from the swap task's target rather than the old htmx:beforeSwap/htmx:afterSettle events. core/core.libraries.yml now aggregates the htmx asset and points at v4.0.0. FormBuilderInterface::HTMX_REQUEST is marked @deprecated in favor of HtmxRequestInfoTrait::isHtmxRequest().

  • Calls removed Htmx methods, replace them, e.g.:
// Before
(new Htmx())->request(['timeout' => 5000]);
// After
(new Htmx())->config(['timeout' => 5000]);
  • Reads the old HTMX request headers directly, switch to the trait or the new header names (HX-Trigger/HX-Trigger-Name are gone, use HX-Source/HX-Request-Type).
  • Listens for Drupal's custom htmx:drupal:load/htmx:drupal:unload events, note the event payload shape may differ since it now derives its target from the htmx 4 swap task queue.
  • Registers an HTMX extension, htmx 4 replaces htmx.defineExtension() with htmx.registerExtension(name, extension) and a flat hook-object shape.

Summary

Previously, calling ModuleHandler::invoke() to run a specific hook for a specific module would throw a LogicException as soon as that module had more than one implementation of the hook, regardless of what those implementations returned. This forced developers to fall back on the more awkward invokeAllWith() just to support a module with multiple hook implementations. Now, invoke() runs all of that module's implementations and merges their results when possible, so code that only needs array results (the common case) works without extra workarounds. The exception is now only raised when the implementations return something that cannot be merged, such as strings or plain objects.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ModuleHandler::invoke() no longer always throws when a module implements the same hook more than once: if every implementation returns NULL, an array, or an \ArrayObject, the results are merged with NestedArray::mergeDeep() and returned; it still throws \LogicException only when a non-mergeable value (e.g. a string or object) is returned.

Technical details

In ModuleHandler::invoke(), the branch handling multiple listeners for a module/hook pair (Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleHandler::invoke()) no longer throws immediately on count($listeners) > 1. Instead it iterates the listeners, skips any that return NULL, and merges array or \ArrayObject results together with NestedArray::mergeDeep(). If a listener returns any other type, the original \LogicException ("Module $module should not implement $hook more than once.") is thrown instead, preserving the old failure mode for non-mergeable results. The interface doc comment on ModuleHandlerInterface::invoke() was updated to document this merging behavior.

A new hidden test module, hook_single_invoke, was added with hook implementations that return arrays, \ArrayObjects, strings, and stdClass objects, used by new tests (testInvokeWithMergeable(), testInvokeWithNotMergeableString(), testInvokeWithNotMergeableClass()) covering both the merge path and the exception path.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

The functions still work exactly as before (they now just delegate internally), so no behavior changes for site visitors, but any custom code calling them directly will start seeing deprecation notices and must be updated ahead of the Drupal 13.0.0 removal.

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Procedural functions file_save_upload(), file_managed_file_save_upload(), and _file_save_upload_from_form() are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed in drupal:13.0.0, replaced by the Drupal\file\Upload\FormFileUploader and Drupal\file\Upload\ManagedFileElementHelper services.

Technical details

The old code mixed API-level file handling with Form API concerns (setting form errors, adding/removing Messenger messages, rendering error lists) in the same functions, which made the logic hard to reuse or test in isolation. This part of the broader #3221796 modernization effort splits that responsibility into two services.

Drupal\file\Upload\FormFileUploader::saveFormUploadedFiles() replaces file_save_upload(). It is the API-level entry point: it pulls uploaded files via UploadedFilesExtractor, delegates the actual move/validate/rename work to FileUploadHandlerInterface::handleFileUpload(), and caches results per form field in the cache.memory bin (keyed file:uploads:<field_name>) instead of the old function-static $upload_cache, so repeated calls within a request return the same result without reprocessing. It owns the Messenger and Renderer dependencies, handling the form-level concerns: collecting per-field validation errors into a single FormStateInterface::setError() call, preserving pre-existing error messages, and calling into FormFileUploader for the actual upload. Summary

Drupal's long-deprecated "Text (formatted, long, with summary)" field type is being carved out of the core text module into its own dedicated, deprecated text_with_summary module, as the final step of removing it from core ahead of Drupal 12. Existing sites that already use this field type (most commonly the body field on nodes) are automatically migrated: an update hook installs the new text_with_summary module when any field of that type is detected, and follow-up update hooks repoint the module dependency on the affected field storage, field, form display, and view display configuration from text to text_with_summary. No manual action is required for a normal update; the field, its data, and its "Summary or trimmed" display option keep working exactly as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: text_with_summary field type/formatter/widget classes in the text module (TextWithSummaryItem, TextSummaryOrTrimmedFormatter, TextareaWithSummaryWidget) are deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and removed in Drupal 12.0.0; use the equivalent classes in the new text_with_summary module instead. The drupal.text asset library in text.module is deprecated the same way.

Technical details

The field type plugin (TextWithSummaryItem), its widget (TextareaWithSummaryWidget), the text_summary_or_trimmed formatter, the associated JS behavior (js/text.js, the summary show/hide toggle), and the corresponding field.field_settings.text_with_summary/field.value.text_with_summary/field.widget.settings.text_textarea_with_summary/field.formatter.settings.text_summary_or_trimmed schema all move into the new core/modules/text_with_summary module (lifecycle: deprecated, depends on drupal:text). The old classes remain in text as thin, @deprecated shims pointing to their text_with_summary counterparts (see #3568381), and TextTrimmedFormatter gained a protected addTrimPreRender() helper so both the text module's own text_trimmed formatter and the new module's text_summary_or_trimmed formatter can share the trimming logic without one depending on the other's field type.

Because text_with_summary depends on text rather than the reverse, text_with_summary uses hook_field_formatter_info_alter() to re-register the text_with_summary field type against text's text_default/text_trimmed formatters, and hook_library_info_alter() to make the text module's drupal.text library (now empty and marked deprecated in text.libraries.yml) depend on text_with_summary/drupal.text, which carries the actual JS.

The migration path lives in text.install's text_update_12001(), which installs text_with_summary only if a field_storage_config of type text_with_summary exists, followed by post-update hooks (text_post_update_update_field_storage_dependencies, ..._field_dependencies, ..._form_display_dependencies, ..._view_display_dependencies, ..._view_dependencies) that use ConfigEntityUpdater to flip the recorded module dependency from text to text_with_summary on each affected config entity. A new TextWithSummaryUpdatePathTest and its fixture (add-text-with-summary-field.php) exercise this path directly since the base update-path fixture no longer ships a text_with_summary field.

use Drupal\text\Plugin\Field\FieldWidget\TextareaWithSummaryWidget;
use Drupal\text\Plugin\Field\FieldFormatter\TextSummaryOrTrimmedFormatter;

use Drupal\text_with_summary\Plugin\Field\FieldType\TextWithSummaryItem;
use Drupal\text_with_summary\Plugin\Field\FieldWidget\TextareaWithSummaryWidget;
use Drupal\text_with_summary\Plugin\Field\FieldFormatter\TextSummaryOrTrimmedFormatter;

Summary

Drupal's locale module previously exposed its internal state (customized vs. non-customized translations, translation source types, overwrite behavior, translation update mode) through a set of global PHP constants defined in locale.module, a pattern core is moving away from as part of modernizing the module. This issue deprecates fourteen of those constants in favor of PHP backed enums and class constants, with no functional change to how translation import, update checking, or the translation settings form behave. Site owners see no change; custom code or contrib modules that reference the old constants directly will start seeing deprecation notices and need to update before Drupal 13.0.0, when the constants are removed.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The constants are replaced according to a fixed mapping: LOCALE_NOT_CUSTOMIZED/LOCALE_CUSTOMIZED become LocaleDefaultOptions::NOT_CUSTOMIZED/LocaleDefaultOptions::CUSTOMIZED; LOCALE_TRANSLATION_USE_SOURCE_LOCAL/LOCALE_TRANSLATION_USE_SOURCE_REMOTE_AND_LOCAL become \Drupal\locale\Model\TranslationUpdateMode::Local/::RemoteAndLocal (both backed by string values, use ->value where a string is expected); LOCALE_TRANSLATION_OVERWRITE_ALL/_NON_CUSTOMIZED/_NONE become \Drupal\locale\Model\Overwrite::All/::NonCustomized/::None; and LOCALE_TRANSLATION_REMOTE/_LOCAL/_CURRENT become \Drupal\locale\Model\SourceType::Remote/::Local/::Current. The TranslationUpdateMode and Overwrite enums use the new OptionsEnumTrait to supply their #options arrays directly to the translation settings form (LocaleSettingsForm), replacing hand-written arrays keyed by the old constants. LOCALE_JS_STRING, LOCALE_JS_OBJECT and LOCALE_JS_OBJECT_CONTEXT have no replacement: their regex patterns are now local variables inlined inside LocaleJs::parseJsFile(). LOCALE_TRANSLATION_STATUS_TTL also has no replacement; its value (600 seconds) is now a literal in TranslationStatusForm::submitForm() pending a follow-up (#3619926) to reconsider the TTL.

LocaleTranslationSource gained three helper methods used throughout the locale codebase to replace direct access to its $type/$files properties: getType() (returns a SourceType enum or NULL), getFile(SourceType $type), and isUpdateAvailable() (true when the type is Local or Remote). Callers such as LocaleFetch, LocaleSource, LocaleProjectChecker and TranslationStatusForm were updated to use these helpers instead of comparing against the old constants or indexing $source->files[LOCALE_TRANSLATION_LOCAL] directly. Summary

Generating the permissions list for the Filter module used to build a link (to the text format's edit page) inside each permission's title. Constructing that link forced Drupal's lazy-built router to rebuild, adding about 500ms to every standard Drupal installation and to any test that installs the Filter module.
